body.statement: Whenever \(\mathcal M_{T_0,T_1}(0)\ne\varnothing\), fix a loading space \(L\) that occurs in that class.  Every decomposition \(z=m+\beta\) with \(m\in L\), \(\lVert m\rVert_2\le A\), \(\lVert\beta\rVert_0\le s\), and \(\lVert\beta\rVert_\infty\le B\) has a unique labeled effect vector \(\beta\) if and only if \(\kappa_s(L)>0\).  If \(\kappa_s(L)=0\), two distinct admissible effect vectors generate the same complete observed-data law with constant post factors.
body.justification: This is the exact identification boundary that makes the margin-indexed inference problem meaningful.
body.gap: ChandrasekaranEtAl2011 and FickusMixon2013 contain the generic sparse-subspace geometry; the causal contribution starts after this supporting equivalence.
body.consumer: It tells applied users when a full labeled direct-and-spillover vector is distinguishable without selecting valid donors.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(P\) be the orthogonal projector onto \(L\).  Suppose first that
\[
z=m_0+\beta_0=m_1+\beta_1
\]
are two admissible decompositions and put \(h=\beta_1-\beta_0\).  The support union has size at most \(2s\), and subtraction gives \(h=m_0-m_1\in L\).  Enlarge \(\operatorname{supp}(h)\), if necessary, to a set \(S\subseteq[N]\) of size \(2s\), and write \(h=E_Sx\).  By the definition of \(\kappa_s(L)\),
\[
0=\lVert(I_N-P)h\rVert_2
=\lVert(I_N-P)E_Sx\rVert_2
\ge \kappa_s(L)\lVert x\rVert_2
=\kappa_s(L)\lVert h\rVert_2.
\]
If \(\kappa_s(L)>0\), this forces \(h=0\), hence \(\beta_0=\beta_1\).

Conversely, if \(\kappa_s(L)=0\), finiteness of the collection of sets \(S\) and compactness of their unit spheres give a nonzero \(h\in L\) with \(\lVert h\rVert_2=1\) and \(|\operatorname{supp}(h)|\le2s\).  Partition its support as \(S_0\mathbin{\dot\cup}S_1\), where \(|S_j|\le s\), and write \(h=h_0+h_1\) with \(h_j\) supported on \(S_j\).  Because \(A,B>0\), one may choose
\[
0<c\le \min\{2A,B/\lVert h\rVert_\infty\}.
\]
Define
\[
\beta_0=-ch_1,
\; \beta_1=ch_0,
\; m_0=ch/2,
\; m_1=-ch/2.
\]
Then both effects are \(s\)-sparse and bounded coordinatewise by \(B\), both latent means belong to \(L\) and have norm at most \(A\), and
\[
m_0+\beta_0={c\over2}(h_0-h_1)=m_1+\beta_1,
\; \beta_1-\beta_0=ch\ne0.
\]
To verify the complete-law assertion, retain any admissible pre-panel parameters having loading space \(L\), the same \(D,F,\sigma\), and the same Gaussian error law.  Since \(D\) is invertible by the positive loading-strength assumption, for \(j=0,1\) choose \(a_j=D^{-1}U^{\top}m_j\) and set \(G_j=a_j\mathbf 1_{T_1}^{\top}\).  These post paths have zero centered covariance and zero centered norm, while \(\Lambda a_j=m_j\).  Their observed post means are equal by the preceding display, their post covariance matrices are both \(\sigma^2I\), and their pre laws are identical.  Thus the full laws of \((Y_0,Y_1)\) coincide although \(\beta_0\ne\beta_1\).  This proves both directions.
